$comment: What each CLI can actually prove about its own lifecycle. Read by TypeScript (fidelity.ts) and by Rust (agent_life.rs, include_str!) so the two can never drift. Every event name here is asserted by src/agentFidelityGuard.test.ts to appear literally inside that CLI's setup_* function in src-tauri/src/agents.rs, and vice versa: a plugin template that renames an event fails CI instead of silently freezing that CLI's state forever. Do not hand-edit a row without re-reading the installer and bumping verifiedAt.

clis.$note: Current Claude emits PermissionRequest plus structured notification_type values; canopy-hook classifies those before the mixed-notification prose fallback retained for older versions. Failure hooks are real turn/tool boundaries too.

PermissionRequest is structural. Native hooks need one-time /hooks trust; the legacy notify fallback now routes through canopy-hook, so it is gated, normalized and pty-stamped rather than writing the bus directly.

Antigravity 1.1.x has no human-prompt hook: Pre/PostInvocation bracket model calls and only prove progress; Stop ends the full execution loop. canopy-hook converts its documented camelCase protojson payload to the canonical wire shape.

One integration total: notifications-command, which aider runs both after a turn and at a y/n confirm. It wants the keyboard and cannot say which kind. Classified attention-only, never "finished" — idle is what auto-hibernation SIGTERMs and what the folded Idle stack hides, and the two failure directions are not symmetric.

These are the normalized names the plugin sends to canopy-hook, not OpenCode's native bus names. Explicit canopy_signal values classify turn start/progress/end and permission at the source so native event renames cannot silently freeze lifecycle state.

The extension maps before_agent_start/agent_settled/session_shutdown and tool approval events onto Canopy's normalized wire names with explicit signals. Installed in omp's auto-discovered agent/extensions directory.

The plugin normalizes agent.start/end and tool.result with explicit lifecycle signals. No reliable permission event is installed, so blocked-on-user remains unprovable and decays to unknown rather than being fabricated.
